<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-beet" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-beet-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of beet, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1 to Q3 spread are required. This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>WHO GEMS/Food is the only compatible sampling family for beet, as sold on this basis in the completed beet ledger, so this single-family reference cannot represent other markets. ## How metals reach beet

<a id="hmi-ing-010"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-root-uptake-surface-deposition-feed-transfer-or-other-biological-pathways"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-011"></a>

<a id="which-source-attribution-claims-are-measured-modelled-inferred-or-unresolved"></a>

The evidence on how metals reach beet comes from studies that compared exposed and ordinary settings. Beet, as sold from Cu100Zn100Pb100 (experiment) had Zn higher at 11,200 µg/kg, against 2,700 µg/kg for control plot, no metal addition, no fertilizer in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/gromakova2017-rostov-root-crop-amendment|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">N. V. Gromakova · 2017</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/gromakova2017-rostov-root-crop-amendment">Yield Assessment of Beetroot and Potato, Cultivated on Ordinary Chernozem Contaminated with Heavy Metals</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Vegetable Crops of Russia 5(38):74–75</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/gromakova2017-rostov-root-crop-amendment">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

These are observational comparisons from single studies; the size of the difference depends on the site, metal and distance.

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-beet" data-anchor="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-beet" data-question="How do heavy metals get into beet?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How do heavy metals get into beet?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In the studies available, beet from contaminated or exposed settings carried more metal than beet from the same study’s control.<sup class="cite">[[sources/gromakova2017-rostov-root-crop-amendment|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">N. V. Gromakova · 2017</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/gromakova2017-rostov-root-crop-amendment">Yield Assessment of Beetroot and Potato, Cultivated on Ordinary Chernozem Contaminated with Heavy Metals</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Vegetable Crops of Russia 5(38):74–75</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/gromakova2017-rostov-root-crop-amendment">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Beet, as sold from Cu100Zn100Pb100 (experiment) had lead higher at 700 µg/kg, against 400 µg/kg for control plot, no metal addition, no fertilizer in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/gromakova2017-rostov-root-crop-amendment|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">N. V. Gromakova · 2017</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/gromakova2017-rostov-root-crop-amendment">Yield Assessment of Beetroot and Potato, Cultivated on Ordinary Chernozem Contaminated with Heavy Metals</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Vegetable Crops of Russia 5(38):74–75</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/gromakova2017-rostov-root-crop-amendment">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-beet" data-anchor="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-beet" data-question="Which regions report the lowest levels in beet?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which regions report the lowest levels in beet?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Among GEMS/Food reporting regions, beet, as sold had the lowest lead subgroup median in PAHO (4.36 µg/kg) and the highest in SEARO (20 µg/kg); reporting regions are markets, not growing areas.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> For cadmium, the lowest regional median was in PAHO (15.3 µg/kg) and the highest in PAHO (16 µg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-beet-is-inorganic" data-anchor="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-beet-is-inorganic" data-question="How much of the arsenic in beet is inorganic?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How much of the arsenic in beet is inorganic?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Inorganic arsenic, the more toxic form, was measured in 1 result from 1 source, far fewer than total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs|10]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) · 2014</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs">Dietary exposure to inorganic arsenic in the European population</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">EFSA Journal 2014;12(3):3597</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) 2014 reported inorganic arsenic at 12.2 µg/kg (mean) in beet, as sold from European dietary-survey occurrence data.<sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs|10]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) · 2014</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs">Dietary exposure to inorganic arsenic in the European population</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">EFSA Journal 2014;12(3):3597</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>
